page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-360-lssd is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance built on AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. It delivers 360 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 180 physical cores using simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 4.0 GB per vCPU, totaling 1440 GB of RAM. The configuration bundles 32 local NVMe SSDs providing 12864 GB of high-speed scratch storage. Vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support are available, alongside hardware acceleration for AES and SHA cryptography.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded throughput and memory capabilities. The instance achieved top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core testing (554,627.01) and PassMark CPU evaluations (157,183.11), complemented by strong single-core ratings. Memory subsystems deliver high sustained throughput, recording 701.37 GB/sec in uncached large-block read testing and 335.55 GB/sec in write operations. Key-value operations also show extreme throughput, evidenced by 398.84 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 138.8 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The bundled local NVMe storage provides significant I/O throughput without reliance on external network-attached disks, making the instance structurally cost-efficient for heavy data ingestion and processing. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for large-scale machine learning training, despite respectable CPU-driven prompt processing throughput. The instance is optimal for distributed database clusters, in-memory caches, large compilation pipelines, and demanding ETL tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-360-lssd is a general-purpose server configuration featuring 360 dedicated vCPUs across 180 physical cores on AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. Designed for data-heavy enterprise tasks, it integrates 1440 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4.0 GB per core ratio, alongside 12864 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity spread across 32 drives. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for multi-core compute throughput, database execution, and memory bandwidth, reaching uncached large-block reads of 701.37 GB/sec and over 398 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware instruction support spans AVX-512, VNNI, and crypto acceleration. While the server lacks discrete GPU accelerators, its substantial compute density and expansive integrated scratch storage offer strong qualitative cost efficiency for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing, and large software build environments.
